body.p: Cuckoo. There lived a woman. She had four children. These children did not listen their mother at all. Once their mother fell ill. She cries to her children: "My children, bring me water." No one of these children said: "It seems, our mother is ill, it seems, she wants water." The mother asks for water again: "My children, bring me water."[ShA:] Kadelaxa and kÉmaraxa are unexpected forms. No one brought her water. After that their mother kept silence. At some point their elder brother came into the house. What does he see? Their mother took floor brooms as her wings, took her thimble as her nose, she became a cuckoo and flew away. These children run behind their mother crying: "Mummy, here's your water." The mother answers: "Cuckoo, cuckoo, but now I don't need water. There is a lot of water in front of me, water from rivers, water from lakes, water from puddles. Now I will find water myself." The children are always running behind their mother and crying: "Mummy, here's your water." In summer or in winter, these children are still running. Blood is coming from their feet. This blood moistens soil and bushes. Where you see red soil, red bushes, this is the blood of these children. This is the end.
